measure: Canopy height before the outbreak, from three sources
basis: The beetle takes large, slowly growing dominants and codominants first [@Massey_1954; @Werner_1983; @Hard_1985b; @Doak_2004], and an outbreak left stands with smaller average and maximum heights [@Veblen_1991]

measure: Sentinel-1 C-band VV level before the outbreak
basis: Backscatter rises with forest biomass until it saturates, C-band being much less sensitive than L-band [@Dobson_1992; @Santoro_2018]
Backscatter rises with biomass to a saturation near 100 tons per hectare at L-band [@Dobson_1992]

measure: Change in VV through the outbreak
expected: A difference of either sign, if the radar recorded the mortality
basis: Radar was proposed for bark beetle damage, although detection before the crowns fade has had limited success [@Hollaus_2019; @Hechtl_2025]

measure: Diameter and height of dead and live white spruce on inventory plots
expected: Dead trees larger and taller where the outbreak has run
basis: Killed trees were larger and grew more slowly than survivors in the same stands [@Werner_1983; @Hard_1985; @Doak_2004]

measure: Year the survey first recorded a stand
basis: The largest trees died first and smaller ones as the outbreak proceeded [@Massey_1954; @Schmid_1976; @Werner_1983]
